subject: Private deployment — network tail latency & throughput next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finedge.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — network tail latency & throughput next steps

Marta — great talk this morning, thanks for carving out the time. Quick recap of the technical/ops items we agreed and the open questions so we can move to a narrow test window: 

- Target SLOs that FinEdge gave us on the call: 95th-percentile end-to-end response tail (streaming first-byte) <= 250ms, sustained throughput goal of 80 requests/sec (avg payload) with concurrency up to 250 simultaneous sessions.
- Redwood ask: produce a short 30–60 minute test window where FinEdge infra runs an iperf3/TCP + UDP check and we run a streaming simulation (synthetic replay) from our private runtime to validate tail latency and rebuffering behavior.
- Network path: agreed to test over the VPN peering path first (site-to-site IPSEC) and, if successful, run a second traceroute over the provider VPC peering link.
- Egress constraints: FinEdge will confirm any outbound port restrictions and whether NAT IPs are static for the test (important for our KV-cache keepalive behavior).
- Acceptance criteria: p95 <= 250ms, no packet loss >0.1% during test, and <5% stream reconnects under the simulated load.

Attached: redwood-private-network-checklist.pdf (checklist we use for private deployments) and private-network-test-plan.xlsx (proposed test steps).

Next steps / proposed timeline:
1) FinEdge infra to confirm test window availability (we suggested Mon/Tue next week, 09:00–12:00 PDT).
2) FinEdge to share NAT/peering IPs + any firewall rules by EOD today so our infra team can pre-whitelist.
3) Redwood to provision a temporary dedicated host in the us-west-2 private sandbox and share ingress endpoints + a short script to spawn the streaming sessions.

If that all sounds right I’ll pull the test artifacts into the HubSpot deal and open the DocuSign for the short test engagement.

Thanks — Mark
Markus Klein
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finedge.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: FinEdge Infra Ops <ops@finedge-infra.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Apr 2027 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — network tail latency & throughput next steps

Thanks Mark — appreciate the concise recap. Two quick clarifications from the infra side: 

1) The 250ms p95 target is for the full round trip from the FinEdge app -> Redwood runtime -> back to client, correct? We want to be explicit because our internal application adds ~30–40ms for TLS and proxying.
2) NATs: our peered VPC uses a set of egress NAT IPs that are mostly static; I’ll confirm the exact list by EOD. For the site-to-site VPN we have dynamic public endpoints but stable internal addressing.

We can do the test window on Monday 2027-05-03 between 09:00–11:30 PDT. Ops will run iperf3. For the streaming replay, can you confirm the expected packet size and whether the test should use TCP-only? We do better on UDP for bulk throughput but production traffic to Redwood will be over TLS/TCP.

Also attaching our internal ops contact (ops@finedge-infra.com) — they will run the traceroutes and collect baseline metrics.

— Marta
Director, Platform Engineering | FinEdge

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finedge.com>, FinEdge Infra Ops <ops@finedge-infra.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Apr 2027 14:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — network tail latency & throughput next steps

Looping you both in to confirm test plan details and to lock down who runs which checks. Priyom / Grace — see Marta’s questions. Summary of how we should split the work: 

- Priyom: build the streaming simulation (TCP/TLS) that matches FinEdge production session behavior. Goal: 20 concurrent streaming sessions at 10 RPS each for 30 minutes (scales to a 250-concurrency run if needed). We want the simulation to emit small-ish frames (~400–1,200 bytes) to stress tail latency rather than raw throughput.
- Grace: coordinate with FinEdge Ops on scheduling and firewall/NAT whitelisting. Confirm whether we need to expose a static public IP for the short test (DocuSign addendum will cover the temporary IP allocation).
- Markus: I’ll prepare the acceptance checklist and the HubSpot test ticket and send the DocuSign link for the short engagement.

Also note: Priyom, please include the following tests in the plan: tcp traceroute (mtr), iperf3 TCP for 5 minutes, iperf3 UDP burst for 1 minute (to measure jitter), and a replayed streaming session with client-side instrumentation (emit p50/p95/p99). We should collect packet captures on the FinEdge side if they can — that will help debug any mid-path MTU or fragmentation issues.

Can you draft the script by EOD Monday so we can run the first test on Tue morning if Monday is blocked?

— Mark

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finedge.com>, FinEdge Infra Ops <ops@finedge-infra.com>
Date: Mon, 02 May 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — network tail latency & throughput next steps

Thanks Mark — I’ve drafted the test artifacts and attached them to the Drive link in the HubSpot ticket. Key technical notes from my review: 

- Simulation characteristics: TLS over TCP, 200–600ms inter-frame interval variance, frame sizes 400–1,200 bytes, keepalive interval 15s to match our runtime. Load profile: ramp 0->100 sessions in 3 minutes, hold for 25 minutes, scale up to 250 sessions for a 10-minute stress burst.
- Measurement points: client-side start-to-first-byte, backend ingest-to-token-emit, and total edge-to-edge. I added an internal RPC budget: keep backend RPCs < 80ms p95 to leave headroom for network tail.
- Network checks included: iperf3 (TCP, 5m), iperf3 (UDP, 1m, 100KB payloads), mtr for 2 minutes, traceroute, and path MTU discovery. I included a small script to automate packet capture start/stop on FinEdge side (requires sudo).
- Known risk: if site-to-site VPN introduces QoS policing or MTU < 1400, we will likely see increased p99 and retransmits; recommend FinEdge Ops check tunnel MTU and enable jumbo frames on the internal path if possible.

I can run a dry run from our sandbox on Tue 08:00–08:30 PDT if you want a low-impact smoke before the full window.

Attachments (Drive): private-network-test-plan.xlsx, redwood-sim-script-v1.sh, slo-budget-diagram.png

— Priyom
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finedge.com>, FinEdge Infra Ops <ops@finedge-infra.com>

Date: Tue, 03 May 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — network tail latency & throughput next steps

Marta — thanks for confirming the Monday window. FinEdge Ops and Redwood have both agreed to the Mon 09:00–11:00 PDT slot; Priyom will run a quick sandbox smoke at 08:15 to verify scripts.

What we need from your side before 16:00 today: 
- NAT IP list (for whitelisting)
- Any firewall egress rules that strip or rewrite TCP options (e.g., MSS clamping)
- Confirmation if packet captures can be taken during the test (pcap) and who on the FinEdge team owns that capture.

I attached the checklist and the test plan to the HubSpot ticket for traceability. After the test, we’ll produce a short writeup with p50/p95/p99 numbers, jitter, and a brief remediation plan if we miss SLOs. If we pass, we’ll outline the next steps for an A/B rollout on your Dedicated host.

Mark — thanks again.
